title: A Wong Kar-wai FILM TITLE QUESTION

commenti.body: As I recall, Happy Together, after a couple of hours of romantic misery, kind of drifts upwards towards in the last ten minutes and ends on this energetic whoosh of hope and positivity - I feel like it's a train hurtling through the lights of Hong Kong? Wasn't Kar-wai simply use the live recording you refer to because it has a suitable celebratory sense of energy and joy? The Turtles versions are laid back in comparison - there's something almost melancholy about the verses. If it's a train rushing into a future of romantic happiness you're after, the Mothers' version is the one.
